q: The sequence of events that involves several different phases and brings about growth and asexual reproduction is called the _____
e: The sequence of events that involves several different phases and brings about growth and asexual reproduction is called the cell cycle. The cell cycle is the ordered sequence of growth, DNA copy, and division. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. Meiosis is different: meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: Interphase is subdivided into which of the following stages?
e: Interphase is subdivided into G1, S, G2. S is the synthesis stage of interphase when DNA is copied. Interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA. Meiosis I, Meiosis II, Cytokinesis is not G1, S, G2.

q: DNA replication occurs during the _____ stage of interphase.
e: DNA replication occurs during the S stage of interphase. DNA replication happens in S phase. S is the synthesis stage of interphase when DNA is copied. G2 is different: g2 is the growth and check stage after DNA has been copied.

q: After DNA replication, each chromosome consists of two identical DNA molecules called _____
e: After DNA replication, each chromosome consists of two identical DNA molecules called chromatids. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Nucleotides is different: nucleotides are the monomers of DNA and RNA.

q: The point where two sister chromatids are joined together is called the _____
e: The point where two sister chromatids are joined together is called the centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. Centrosome is not centromere.

q: During the G$_2$ stage of interphase, the cell prepares for division by replicating _____
e: During the G2 stage of interphase, the cell prepares for division by replicating organelles. Interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA. DNA is different: dNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: The phase of the cell cycle that involves active nuclear division is called _____
e: The phase of the cell cycle that involves active nuclear division is called mitosis. Mitosis divides the nucleus so two daughter nuclei get identical chromosomes. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. Interphase is different: interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA.

q: Cytokinesis refers to the separation of the _____
e: Cytokinesis refers to the separation of the cytoplasm. Cytoplasm is the fluid and structures inside the cell membrane, around the nucleus. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells.

q: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by the formation of a _____
e: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by the formation of a cleavage furrow. Animal cells pinch in a cleavage furrow during cytokinesis. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Spindle fiber is not cleavage furrow.

q: In plant cells, cytokinesis involves the formation of a _____
e: In plant cells, cytokinesis involves the formation of a cell plate. Plant cells build a cell plate to divide the cytoplasm. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Centrosome is not cell plate.

q: The first phase of mitosis is _____
e: The first phase of mitosis is prophase. In prophase chromosomes condense and the spindle starts to form. Mitosis divides the nucleus so two daughter nuclei get identical chromosomes. Anaphase is different: in anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

q: During prophase of mitosis, the _____ breaks down and the nucleolus disappears.
e: During prophase of mitosis, the nuclear envelope breaks down and the nucleolus disappears. The nuclear envelope breaks down in prophase and reforms in telophase. The nucleolus vanishes in prophase and returns in telophase. Cell membrane is not nuclear envelope.

q: Radial arrays of microtubules around each centriole are called _____
e: Radial arrays of microtubules around each centriole are called asters. Asters are microtubule arrays around the poles in animal mitosis. Kinetochores is not asters.

q: During metaphase of mitosis, chromosomes line up along the _____
e: During metaphase of mitosis, chromosomes line up along the metaphase plate. The metaphase plate is the equator where chromosomes align. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Cleavage furrow is different: animal cells pinch in a cleavage furrow during cytokinesis.

q: Each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its _____
e: Each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids stay attached at the centromere. Nucleolus is different: the nucleolus vanishes in prophase and returns in telophase.

q: In anaphase of mitosis, sister chromatids are pulled apart when the _____ divide.
e: In anaphase of mitosis, sister chromatids are pulled apart when the centromeres divide. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. In anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles. Spindles is not centromeres.

q: At the end of anaphase, the separated chromatids are now called _____
e: At the end of anaphase, the separated chromatids are now called chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. Centrioles is not chromosomes.

q: During telophase, nuclear envelopes _____ around the two sets of chromosomes.
e: During telophase, nuclear envelopes reform around the two sets of chromosomes. Two nuclear envelopes form in telophase. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Duplicate is not reform.

q: The result of mitosis and cytokinesis is two _____ daughter cells.
e: The result of mitosis and cytokinesis is two genetically identical daughter cells. Mitosis makes genetically identical body cells for growth and repair. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells. Genetically different is not genetically identical.

q: Meiosis occurs only in the _____
e: Meiosis occurs only in the sex organs. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Somatic cells is not sex organs.

q: Meiosis is also known as _____ division.
e: Meiosis is also known as reduction division. Chromosome number is reduced in meiosis I, not in mitosis. Equational is not reduction.

q: In animals, the formation of sperm is called _____
e: In animals, the formation of sperm is called spermatogenesis. Spermatogenesis is meiosis that produces sperm. Oogenesis is different: oogenesis is meiosis that produces eggs.

q: In flowering plants, meiosis produces microspores and megaspores that develop into _____
e: In flowering plants, meiosis produces microspores and megaspores that develop into gametes. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms. Zygotes is not gametes.

q: Meiosis involves _____ nuclear divisions.
e: Meiosis involves two nuclear divisions. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Three is different: dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: The pairing of homologous chromosomes during prophase I is called _____
e: The pairing of homologous chromosomes during prophase I is called synapsis. Synapsis is pairing of homologous chromosomes in meiosis I. Homologous chromosomes pair in meiosis; they carry the same genes but may have different alleles. Segregation is different: segregation is the splitting of allele pairs when gametes form.

q: Genetic variation is introduced during prophase I by _____
e: Genetic variation is introduced during prophase I by crossing over. Crossing over in prophase I swaps DNA between homologous chromosomes. Meiosis, crossing over, and random fertilisation generate genetic variation. Cytokinesis is different: cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells.

q: During metaphase I of meiosis, _____ line up on the metaphase plate.
e: During metaphase I of meiosis, pairs of homologous chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate. Independent assortment concerns different pairs of homologous chromosomes. Homologous chromosomes pair in meiosis; they carry the same genes but may have different alleles. Sister chromatids is not pairs of homologous chromosomes.

q: In anaphase I of meiosis, the _____ do not divide.
e: In anaphase I of meiosis, the centromeres do not divide. In anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Nuclear envelopes is different: two nuclear envelopes form in telophase.

q: At the end of meiosis I, each daughter cell is _____
e: At the end of meiosis I, each daughter cell is haploid. Haploid cells have one set of chromosomes, as in gametes. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Tetraploid is not haploid.

q: No _____ occurs between meiosis I and meiosis II.
e: No chromosome replication occurs between meiosis I and meiosis II. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Meiosis halves the chromosome number for gametes. Spindle formation is not chromosome replication.

q: The branch of biology that deals with the inheritance of characteristics from parents to progeny is called _____
e: The branch of biology that deals with the inheritance of characteristics from parents to progeny is called genetics. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms. Evolution is not genetics.

q: The physical and chemical characteristics that make up the appearance of an organism are known as its _____
e: The physical and chemical characteristics that make up the appearance of an organism are known as its phenotype. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment. Genotype is different: genotype is the allele combination an organism carries.

q: The total combination of genes and their alleles received from an individual’s parents is called the _____
e: The total combination of genes and their alleles received from an individual’s parents is called the genotype. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. Karyotype is not genotype.

q: Units of hereditary characteristics located on chromosomes are called _____
e: Units of hereditary characteristics located on chromosomes are called genes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Alleles is different: alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: Different forms of the same gene are known as _____
e: Different forms of the same gene are known as alleles. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. A gene is a DNA stretch that codes for a product, usually a protein. Chromosomes is different: chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: An individual with two identical alleles for a gene is said to be _____
e: An individual with two identical alleles for a gene is said to be homozygous. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. Hemizygous is not homozygous.

q: An individual with two different alleles for a gene is said to be _____
e: An individual with two different alleles for a gene is said to be heterozygous. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. Homozygous recessive is not heterozygous.

q: Mendel’s first law is also known as the law of _____
e: Mendel’s first law is also known as the law of segregation. Segregation is the splitting of allele pairs when gametes form. Independent assortment is different: independent assortment is the random sorting of different chromosome pairs into gametes.

q: According to Mendel’s law of segregation, the two alleles for a trait separate during the formation of _____
e: According to Mendel’s law of segregation, the two alleles for a trait separate during the formation of gametes. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis. Segregation is the splitting of allele pairs when gametes form. Zygotes is not gametes.

q: A monohybrid cross demonstrates Mendel’s principle of _____
e: A monohybrid cross demonstrates Mendel’s principle of segregation. Segregation is the splitting of allele pairs when gametes form. Independent assortment is different: independent assortment is the random sorting of different chromosome pairs into gametes.

q: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous purple-flowered pea plants (Pp × Pp), the phenotypic ratio in the F$_2$ generation is _____
e: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous purple-flowered pea plants (Pp × Pp), the phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation is 3:1. A monohybrid heterozygous cross gives a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. 9:3:3:1 is different: a dihybrid heterozygous cross gives the classic 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio.

q: Mendel’s second law is also known as the law of _____
e: Mendel’s second law is also known as the law of independent assortment. Independent assortment is the random sorting of different chromosome pairs into gametes. Dominance is not independent assortment.

q: The law of independent assortment applies when genes are located on _____
e: The law of independent assortment applies when genes are located on different pairs of homologous chromosomes. Independent assortment concerns different pairs of homologous chromosomes. Independent assortment is the random sorting of different chromosome pairs into gametes. Mitochondrial DNA is not different pairs of homologous chromosomes.

q: In a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous individuals (RrYy × RrYy), the F$_2$ phenotypic ratio is _____
e: In a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous individuals (RrYy × RrYy), the F2 phenotypic ratio is 9:3:3:1. A dihybrid heterozygous cross gives the classic 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. 1:1:1:1 is not 9:3:3:1.

q: A testcross is used to determine the genotype of an individual with a _____ phenotype.
e: A testcross is used to determine the genotype of an individual with a dominant phenotype. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment. Codominant is different: codominant alleles both show fully in the heterozygote, as in AB blood.

q: In a testcross, the unknown individual is always crossed with a _____ individual.
e: In a testcross, the unknown individual is always crossed with a homozygous recessive individual. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same. A recessive allele shows only when two copies are present. Homozygous dominant is not homozygous recessive.

q: If a tall pea plant (unknown genotype) is testcrossed with a dwarf (tt) and all offspring are tall, the tall parent is _____
e: If a tall pea plant (unknown genotype) is testcrossed with a dwarf (tt) and all offspring are tall, the tall parent is TT. Tt is homozygous recessive. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries.

q: A backcross involves mating F$_1$ progeny back to _____
e: A backcross involves mating F1 progeny back to one of their parents. Another F1 is not one of their parents.

q: Codominant alleles are both _____ in the heterozygous condition.
e: Codominant alleles are both observed phenotypically in the heterozygous condition. Observed size over actual size gives magnification. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. Blended is not observed phenotypically.

q: In Shorthorn cattle, the genotype C$^R$C$^W$ produces a _____ coat color.
e: In Shorthorn cattle, the genotype C^RC^W produces a roan coat color. Roan coat is a classic codominance of red and white hairs. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries.

q: Incomplete dominance results in a _____ of the two homozygous phenotypes.
e: Incomplete dominance results in a blending of the two homozygous phenotypes. Incomplete dominance blends the heterozygote, as in pink from red and white. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same. Mixture is not blending.

q: When two pink-flowered snapdragons (RW) are crossed, the phenotypic ratio is _____
e: When two pink-flowered snapdragons (RW) are crossed, the phenotypic ratio is 1 red: 2 pink: 1 white. Incomplete dominance in a heterozygous cross gives 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: When more than two alleles exist for a gene in a population, it is referred to as _____
e: When more than two alleles exist for a gene in a population, it is referred to as multiple alleles. Multiple alleles means a gene has more than two possible versions in the population, as in ABO blood groups. A population is all the individuals of one species in an area. Epistasis is not multiple alleles.

q: In the ABO blood group system, the alleles I$^A$ and I$^B$ are _____ to each other.
e: In the ABO blood group system, the alleles I^A and I^B are codominant to each other. Codominant alleles both show fully in the heterozygote, as in AB blood. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene. Incompletely dominant is not codominant.

q: The blood group that is the universal donor is _____
e: The blood group that is the universal donor is O. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene. O is the universal donor for red cells because it lacks A and B antigens. B is not O.

q: The blood group that is the universal recipient is _____
e: The blood group that is the universal recipient is AB. AB blood is codominance of IA and IB alleles. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene. O is not AB.

q: Individuals with blood group O have _____ in their plasma.
e: Individuals with blood group O have both anti-A and anti-B in their plasma. Group O plasma has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene.

q: In mammals, males are chromosomally _____
e: In mammals, males are chromosomally XY. XY is the typical human male sex-chromosome pair; the Y carries maleness factors. XX is different: xX is the typical human female sex-chromosome pair.

q: In humans, the heterogametic sex is the _____
e: In humans, the heterogametic sex is the male. Human males are heterogametic because they make X and Y sperm. Female is not male.

q: The expected sex ratio in human offspring is _____
e: The expected sex ratio in human offspring is 1 female: 1 male. 1 female : 1 male is the biological term this statement needs.

q: A change in a gene or chromosome that may cause a change in a phenotypic characteristic is called a _____
e: A change in a gene or chromosome that may cause a change in a phenotypic characteristic is called a mutation. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Variation is not mutation.

q: Only mutations in _____ can be passed on to the next generation.
e: Only mutations in sex cells can be passed on to the next generation. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. Somatic cells is not sex cells.

q: Trisomy of chromosome 21 causes _____
e: Trisomy of chromosome 21 causes Down’s syndrome. Down's syndrome comes from an extra chromosome 21. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Albinism is not Down’s syndrome.

q: Down’s syndrome is more common in babies born to women over _____ years of age.
e: Down’s syndrome is more common in babies born to women over 40 years of age. Down's syndrome comes from an extra chromosome 21. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome. 35 is not 40.

q: A change in the nucleotide sequence of a DNA molecule is termed a _____
e: A change in the nucleotide sequence of a DNA molecule is termed a gene mutation. A gene mutation changes the base sequence of one gene. A nucleotide is a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogen base. Chromosome mutation is not gene mutation.

q: Albinism is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the enzyme that produces _____
e: Albinism is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the enzyme that produces melanin. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Insulin is different: insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar.

q: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the _____ protein.
e: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the CFTR protein. CFTR is a chloride-channel protein; its failure causes cystic fibrosis. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Collagen is not CFTR.

q: Sickle-cell anemia is caused by a mutation in the gene for the _____ of hemoglobin.
e: Sickle-cell anemia is caused by a mutation in the gene for the β-chain of hemoglobin. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. A gene is a DNA stretch that codes for a product, usually a protein.

q: Huntington’s disease is caused by a mutation in the HD gene located on chromosome _____
e: Huntington’s disease is caused by a mutation in the HD gene located on chromosome 4. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. X is not 4.

q: Agents that cause mutations are called _____
e: Agents that cause mutations are called mutagens. Physical mutagens include radiation; chemical mutagens include some drugs and pollutants. Teratogens is not mutagens.

q: Ultra-violet radiation, X-rays, and gamma rays are examples of _____
e: Ultra-violet radiation, X-rays, and gamma rays are examples of physical mutagens. Physical mutagens include radiation; chemical mutagens include some drugs and pollutants. Biophysics uses physical laws; it is not the same as biochemistry. Biological mutagens is not physical mutagens.

q: Variation is the _____ that exist within a species.
e: Variation is the differences that exist within a species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring. Mutations is not differences.

q: Continuous variation shows _____ between traits of a characteristic.
e: Continuous variation shows no clear-cut distinction between traits of a characteristic. Continuous culture keeps adding nutrients and taking product for a long run.

q: Discontinuous variation shows a _____ between two traits.
e: Discontinuous variation shows a clear-cut distinction between two traits. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Gradual transition is not clear-cut distinction.

q: Continuous variation is usually caused by _____
e: Continuous variation is usually caused by polygenic effects. Polygenic traits are controlled by many genes and often show continuous variation. Continuous culture keeps adding nutrients and taking product for a long run. Single gene effects is not polygenic effects.

q: Discontinuous variation is usually controlled by _____
a: a single gene with different alleles
e: Discontinuous variation is usually controlled by a single gene with different alleles. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. A gene is a DNA stretch that codes for a product, usually a protein. Multiple genes is not a single gene with different alleles.

q: Features which enable organisms to survive in their environment are called _____
e: Features which enable organisms to survive in their environment are called adaptations. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. Variations is not adaptations.

q: Adaptations can be classified as anatomical, physiological, or _____
e: Adaptations can be classified as anatomical, physiological, or behavioral. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment. Morphological is not behavioral.

q: The presence of closable nostrils in camels is an example of a(n) _____ adaptation.
e: The presence of closable nostrils in camels is an example of a(n) anatomical adaptation. Anatomical adaptations are structural, such as thick fur or a flattened leaf. Behavioral is not anatomical.

q: A camel’s ability to vary its body temperature over 6°C is a _____ adaptation.
e: A camel’s ability to vary its body temperature over 6°C is a physiological adaptation. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water. Anatomical is different: anatomical adaptations are structural, such as thick fur or a flattened leaf.

q: Camels lying down together to minimize sun exposure is a _____ adaptation.
e: Camels lying down together to minimize sun exposure is a behavioral adaptation. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome. Physiological is different: physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water.

q: Natural selection is the process by which well-adapted organisms have a greater chance to _____
e: Natural selection is the process by which well-adapted organisms have a greater chance to breed and pass on alleles. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. Mutate is not breed and pass on alleles.

q: The theory of natural selection was first proposed by _____
e: The theory of natural selection was first proposed by Charles Darwin. Darwin's evolution by natural selection is a core theme of biology. Louis Pasteur is not Charles Darwin.

q: Artificial selection is also called _____
e: Artificial selection is also called selective breeding. Random mating is not selective breeding.

q: In artificial selection, selection is due to _____
e: In artificial selection, selection is due to human influences. Environmental factors is not human influences.

q: Compared to natural selection, artificial selection is a _____ process.
e: Compared to natural selection, artificial selection is a faster process. Slower is not faster.

q: In artificial selection, inbreeding is common and often leads to _____
e: In artificial selection, inbreeding is common and often leads to loss of vigour. Hybrid vigour is not loss of vigour.

q: Natural selection may lead to _____
e: Natural selection may lead to new species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring. Loss of all variation is not new species.

q: ‘Nature’ refers to all the _____ that influence physical characteristics.
e: ‘Nature’ refers to all the genes and hereditary factors that influence physical characteristics. Accidents and scars is not genes and hereditary factors.

q: ‘Nurture’ refers to all the _____ that impact on character.
e: ‘Nurture’ refers to all the environmental variables that impact on character. Genes inherited from parents is not environmental variables.

q: An apple tree seed will never grow into an oak tree because of _____
e: An apple tree seed will never grow into an oak tree because of genetic variation. Meiosis, crossing over, and random fertilisation generate genetic variation. Seed plants are gymnosperms and angiosperms. Artificial selection is not genetic variation.

q: A scar from an accident is an example of _____ variation.
e: A scar from an accident is an example of environmental variation. Genetic is not environmental.

q: Genetically identical plants grown under different light conditions look different due to _____
e: Genetically identical plants grown under different light conditions look different due to environmental variation. Mitosis makes genetically identical body cells for growth and repair. Meiosis is different: meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.
